title: On a problem of Sivaraman and a problem of Gyárfás
summary: The \textit{girth} of a graph $G$, denoted $\mathrm{g}(G)$, is the length of a shortest cycle in $G$. If $G$ contains no cycle, we define $\mathrm{g}(G)=\infty$. Sivaraman (2020) asked for the optimal $χ$-bounding function for the class of graphs whose complements have girth at least $6$. Let \(F(s) = \max\{χ(G): ω(G)\le s,\ \mathrm{g}(\overline{G})\ge 6\}\). We prove that there exists a constant \(c>0\) such that \[ c\left(\frac{s}{\log s}\right)^{4/3} \le F(s) \le (1+o(1))\frac{s^{3/2}}{\log s}. \] For small values, we establish the exact results \[ F(1)=1,\; F(2)=2,\; F(3)=4,\; F(4)=5,\;…
